text:
anya: heads up — canary bring-up for hammerhead13b (int4) showing ~25% throughput regression vs float16 and occasional OOMs on long prompts (>800 tokens). started at 09:12 PT.
liam: can you paste the canary config and a sample log snippet? also which quant pipeline did we use (per-channel, per-tensor)?
anya: using `int4-perchannel-legacy` (the quick quantize job). canary config below. logs show CUDA OOMs in the kv-cache alloc path.
```
model: hammerhead13b
variant: int4-perchannel-legacy
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  max_concurrent: 8
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 1024
  warmup_slots: 2
allocator:
  type: cuda_malloc
  soft_reserve: 0.06
  compactor: disabled
```
liam: interesting — high `max_new_tokens` + cuda_malloc soft_reserve low. frag issues are common when we concat long prompts. can you attach a stacktrace?
anya: stacktrace snippet: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.2 GiB for kv_cache` (happens after ~3rd generation window).
samir: quick hypotheses: 1) allocator fragmentation from cuda_malloc + large dynamic allocations, 2) default max_new_tokens too high for canary batch mix, 3) quant kernel micro-scheduling causing transient high peak allocations.
perf-bench-bot: bench results (canary vs baseline, median of 50 runs):
- float16 baseline: 310 req/s, p95 latency 210ms
- int4 canary (current): 235 req/s, p95 latency 280ms, 5 OOMs per 50 runs
audrey: can we rule out quality regression first? int4-perchannel-legacy had mild token-level shift in evals last week. worth running the eval harness for top-5 prompts.
anya: starting eval now (kickoff command):
```
rwdctl eval run --model hammerhead13b:int4-perchannel-legacy --suite /evals/conv-quality/scale10 --out /tmp/hh13b-int4-eval.json
```
ops: also add metric for fragmentation ratio (cuda_malloc_free/alloc_count) to the canary dashboard — I'm seeing the ratio spike right before OOMs in other models. will patch dashboard. :eyes:
liam: proposed immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact:
- lower default `max_new_tokens` to 256 for int4 canary
- bump `soft_reserve` to 0.12 and enable compactor (slot compaction every 30s)
- set `batching.max_concurrent` to 6 to reduce concurrency peaks
- add a kernel-sched hint `allow_tail_spill: false` for the int4 path (temp)
samir: sounds good. also suggest enabling a short warmstart: `warmup_slots: 4` to pre-touch KV pages and reduce malloc churn.
anya: applying a canary patch now (command):
```
rwdctl rollout update --model hammerhead13b:int4-perchannel-legacy --set defaults.max_new_tokens=256 --set allocator.soft_reserve=0.12 --set allocator.compactor=enabled --set batching.max_concurrent=6 --set defaults.warmup_slots=4
```
perf-bench-bot: quick smoke after config change (10 runs): median 290 req/s, p95 220ms, 0 OOMs observed in smoke.
audrey: after the patch we should gate the full rollout on eval delta < 0.5% RAL (response agreement) and manual QA on 20 queries. I'll run the eval harness output diff and post results.
ops: keeping an eye on fragmentation metric for the next 2 hours and will auto-scale to a spare pool if OOM rate > 1% in canary.
liam: follow-ups: @anya pls capture a heap profile pre/post compactor (cuda heap + slab) and upload, @samir can you run a microbench isolating kernel scheduling for int4 path? I'll create a perf issue to track.
anya: ack — uploading heap profile to /internal/bench/hh13b/7384659123/ and will ping when done.
samir: thanks. if the compactor + warmup fix holds, we can roll to dedicated canary and then staged rollouts. if not, fallback plan is swap to `int8-mixed` for the model until we root cause. :thumbsup:
ops: noted. will alert on-call if OOMs resume.
anya: final note — no quality regression in the 20-query QA so far, int4 token diffs within expected noise. continuing monitoring. :white_check_mark:
